about: Lane B's recall selection: which rule corpora, directories, rule files and native-analyser rules Lane B runs, and which paths it never reports from. Decided by the owner on 2026-10-03 from the per-rule counts in eval/results/candidates-per-scan.json. data/rules/MANIFEST.json is generated from this file by `python -m anvil_eval.vendor_rules` and internal/recall verifies both.

tools.name: opengrep
tools.licence_evidence: eval/tools/opengrep/LICENSES.md section 1, the LICENSE body at tag v1.26.0
tools.role: runs the vendored rule corpora; subprocess only

tools.name: bandit
tools.licence_evidence: the LICENSE body at tag 1.9.4, read 2026-10-03

excluded_directories.reason: Every one of its 62 rule files is headed 'License: GPL 2.0': they are generated from flawfinder, which is GPL-2.0. The repository LICENSE keeps third-party components under their own licences. Excluded by the owner on 2026-10-03; C coverage comes from 0xdea's MIT rules.
Its one rule, bad-words, flags comments (CWE-546) and its author lists it as 'potentially too noisy and unsuitable for general use'. It was 5,249 of curl's 10,714 candidates.

excluded_rule_files.reason: Assert statements (CWE-754), the same informational finding as bandit B101.
A code-review heuristic: lists calls worth a look (CWE-676), not a weakness. 1,440 of curl's candidates outside its tests.
A code-review heuristic for operator typos (CWE-480). 977 of curl's candidates outside its tests.
A code-review heuristic flagging every signed-to-unsigned conversion (CWE-195). 493 of curl's candidates outside its tests.
A code-review heuristic for assert usage (CWE-754).
A code-quality pattern (CWE-478), not a weakness.
A code-review heuristic (CWE-469) flagging every pointer subtraction.
A code-quality pattern (CWE-484), not a weakness.
A code-quality pattern (CWE-393), not a weakness.
A code-review heuristic marking every argv and envp access (CWE-15).
A code-review heuristic for high-entropy string literals (CWE-540).

Its companion test file states no licence, and GitLab's mappings tie it to a find-sec-bugs rule id (an LGPL-3.0 analyser), so nothing but its own MIT header speaks for it. Dropped by the owner on 2026-10-04, after the same-family review.

exclude_by_derived_licence.decided: the owner, 2026-10-03, after the same-family review (docs/reviews/lane-b-gate.md)
exclude_by_derived_licence.reason: GitLab ported most of its rules from other analysers and labels each rule's companion test file with the upstream licence. 131 rules headed 'MIT (c) GitLab Inc.' have companions labelled 'LGPL-3.0 License (c) find-sec-bugs' (Java 42, Scala 68) or '(c) security-code-scan' (C# 21). A rule's licence is the stricter of the two headers, and rules derived under LGPL-3.0 are left out; the manifest lists each one.

excluded_tool_rules.reason: Assert statements (CWE-703): informational. 1,054 of flask's 1,090 candidates.

excluded_paths.reason: Lane B reports on shipped first-party code. Test, test-data, documentation and example trees are not shipped; they were 1,071 of flask's 1,090 candidates and 2,131 of curl's 10,714.
